method.label: Pair numbers summing to the maximum

annotationRationale: An explicit ten-element construction attains the bound. Pairing around the largest element gives a pigeonhole-style upper bound, with the even middle element handled separately.
sourceMethod: Follows the official construction-and-pairing argument. Separate even and odd cases make the pair counts and the exclusion of a possible middle element explicit.

review.mathCheck: For maximum m, complementary pairs permit at most one selected member; when m is even, m/2 is forbidden. Thus the size is at most the ceiling of m/2, hence at most 10. The set {11,...,20} attains 10 because every pairwise sum is at least 22. Choice C is correct.
review.sourceMethodCheck: An originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA Problem 21's construction and pairing-around-the-maximum argument. The explicit parity split correctly handles the repeated-addend restriction and makes the official upper bound reconstructible.
review.annotationCheck: Both the extremal bound with an attaining construction and the pigeonhole-style pairing bound are assessed. No unused direct concept or material gap.
